title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X is the Deligne–Mumford compactification of M_{g,ν}, viewed as a stack or orbifold, with the boundary normal-crossings divisor. The divisor stratifies X into closed strata D_{d_α} with open parts D^*_{d_α}. For pairs of strata, V^{d'_0}_{d_α,d''_0} denote the deleted tubular-neighbourhood ('link') spaces. On the previous page Grothendieck identified the fundamental groupoid of the deleted normal-cone bundle over D^*_{d_*} with Π_1 V. Via the homotopy exact sequence, that groupoid is an extension of π_1 of the stratum by a quotient of Z^r (the quotient by the image of π_2).

This page (Remarque, p.85) assumes every open stratum D^*_{d_α} is a K(π,1). This holds in the Teichmüller case: boundary strata are finite quotients of products of moduli stacks M_{g',ν'}, which are K(π,1) because Teichmüller space is contractible. Grothendieck then claims the following. The diagram formed by the fundamental groupoids Π_1 V^{d'_0}_{d_α,d''_0}, together with the canonical morphisms between them, should reconstruct:
(i) the (pro-)fundamental groupoid of X and of the various canonical topoi attached to X;
(ii) the 'quasi-geometric' topos of sheaves on X whose restriction to each elementary (constitutive) stratum-topos is locally constant, i.e. the topos of stratified-constructible sheaves of sets, glued by recollement;
(iii) through (ii), the homotopy types of the 'neighbouring' topoi, X included.

The 'Remords' and the vertical margin note retract (iii). What the K(π,1) data should reconstruct are the homotopy types of the neighbouring topoi, not by itself the homotopy type of X via the constructible 1-topos. The next page gives the counterexample X = P^1 = S^2 with D = {∞}:
- The group data form the diagram {1} ← Z → {1}.
- The topos of sheaves locally constant on C = P^1∖{∞} is the presheaf topos on the category •→•.
- That category has a final object, so the topos is cohomologically trivial, whereas H^2(S^2) ≠ 0.
Grothendieck concludes by raising the general problem of the homotopy type of a topos obtained by recollement of an open subtopos and its closed complement.

Modern reading. Constructible sheaves of sets see only the homotopy 1-category of exit paths. In it, Hom(∞, x) = π_0(link S^1) = point, which collapses the information. The exit-path ∞-category (MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie) keeps the mapping space S^1, and its groupoidification is the homotopy pushout pt ← S^1 → pt = S^2. Equivalently, the homotopy colimit of the diagram of classifying spaces of the groupoids {1} ← Z → {1} correctly recovers S^2. So the groupoid data suffice for the homotopy type; the 1-topos built from it does not.
errors: Claim (iii), that the topos of sheaves locally constant on each stratum determines the homotopy type of X (and of the other neighbouring topoi), is false in general. Grothendieck retracts it himself in the 'Remords' and the margin, and the next page gives the S^2 counterexample. The topos of stratum-wise locally constant sheaves of sets loses the higher homotopy of the links.
Minor: in claim (i), recovering π_1(X) from the link groupoids requires the van Kampen gluing along the whole stratification diagram, which the page only sketches. Correct in substance.

ideas.what: Boundary strata of M̄_{g,ν} are K(π,1) (as orbifolds or stacks), so homotopy-theoretic data at infinity reduce to groupoid data
ideas.modern_name: Asphericity of moduli stacks M_{g,n} and of boundary strata (products of these modulo finite groups)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Teichmüller theory; Bers, Earle–Eells); used in Ivanov, Harer, Charney–Lee, etc.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, M_{g,ν} as K(π,1) stacks)

ideas.what: Reconstructing the fundamental (pro)groupoid of a stratified space from the diagram of fundamental groupoids of strata and of their deleted tubular neighbourhoods
ideas.modern_name: van Kampen theorem for stratified spaces; exit-path / stratified fundamental groupoid
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (exit paths, 1990s, unpublished), Treumann (2009), Woolf; Lurie HA Appendix A
ideas.where_published: Possibly in spirit in Esquisse d'un programme, §5 on 'dévissage' of stratified structures; not in this form

ideas.what: Topos of sheaves locally constant on each stratum, glued by recollement ('topos quasi-géométrique / quasi-galoisien'), equivalent to representations of a category of strata and links
ideas.modern_name: Constructible sheaves with respect to a stratification as functors on the exit-path category (1-categorical version); recollement of topoi
ideas.where_published: SGA4 Exp. IV (recollement of open/closed subtopoi); the specific use here is unpublished

ideas.what: The homotopy type of a recollement 1-topos is not the homotopy pushout of the pieces: the constructible 1-topos of (S^2, point) is contractible
ideas.modern_name: Failure of 1-truncated constructible topos to model the stratified homotopy type; repaired by exit-path ∞-categories / ∞-topos recollement
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Lurie HA A.9 and Treumann; folklore
ideas.where_published: Not known in published texts; the motivation resembles Pursuing Stacks (1983)

missed.claim: Grothendieck pinpoints precisely why set-valued constructible sheaves cannot recover the homotopy type of a stratified space: the link homotopy is truncated to π_0. He then asks for a theory of the homotopy type of recollement topoi. This is exactly the gap later filled by exit-path ∞-categories and ∞-topos recollement. It also shows the groupoid diagram he wrote down (e.g. {1} ← Z → {1}) does carry the correct homotopy type via its homotopy colimit, so the right object is the diagram, not the 1-topos.
missed.quote: Remords Ce n'est pas le cas ... ce qui doit se reconstituer à partir de ces K(π,1), ce sont les types d'homotopie des topos voisins...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a precursor, in the moduli-of-curves setting, of the stratified-homotopy and exit-path philosophy. It explains a historical route from the 'structure à l'infini' of M̄_{g,ν} to the higher-stack concerns of Pursuing Stacks.

missed.claim: Programme: describe the homotopy type of M̄_{g,ν} (as a stack, or profinitely) as the homotopy colimit of the diagram of link groupoids Π_1 V of the boundary strata. Here the strata are K(π,1) and the links are torus-bundle extensions by Z^r quotients.
missed.quote: la connaissance des système des π_1 V^{d'_0}_{d_α,d''_0} précédents (avec les morphismes canoniques entre ces groupoïdes) doit permettre de reconstituer ... le (pro)groupoïde fondamental de X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Related to later work on the homotopy type of the Deligne–Mumford compactification (e.g. Ebert–Giansiracusa) and to profinite/Galois actions on boundary-stratified data (Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory). An explicit hocolim-of-groupoids model of M̄_{g,n} indexed by stable graphs is close to known constructions but not attributed to this source.

deep.surprise_reason: The general programme of dévissage of stratified structures and the Teichmüller-tower outlook are known from the Esquisse. The explicit self-correction is a nice early insight not documented in the published record: 1-topos recollement loses link homotopy, shown by the S^2 example, together with the question of the homotopy type of recollement topoi. It anticipates exit-path ∞-categories, but it is a remark rather than a developed result.
transcription_corrections: 'la connaissance des système' should read 'la connaissance du système' (or 'des systèmes').

The insertion 'divers' replaces the crossed-out 'topos' on the line above, giving 'et des divers topos canoniques associés à X'.
The final lines are uncertain. Possibly 'Remords Ce n'est pas le cas pour [?] ... sans topos supplémentaires, par une raison [?]'; the next page continues with 'compte – le cas le plus simple ...'.
